info.name: BaaS Merchant API
info.description:
The BaaS API supports two distinct environments: Live and Test (Sandbox). Understanding the difference between these environments is essential for a smooth integration process.

- **Test Environment (Sandbox):** This environment is designed exclusively for testing purposes, using simulated data to replicate real-world scenarios without any financial impact. It allows you to test and validate your integration before going live.
    
- **Production Environment (Live):** This envrionment is a live enviroment thats only accessbilbe after doing all the neccessary integrations and KYB compliance checks and approval.
    

**Note: Keep scrolling to see full documentation guidelines**

item.name: Registration and Onboarding
item.description: **Step 1:** A new Merchant should visit [https://baas.getrova.com/](https://baas.getrova.com/) to create a new BaaS account for their organization **Step 2:** In the process of creating an account, you're required to proceed through the process of "Profile Creation" and verifiying your idenity information to complete through the onboarding journey After successfully creating an Account, you'll land on the dashboard to get started **Step 3: Under the API catalog Module** You're required pick any of the APIs services under the Solution groups and subscribe to them one by one. Ensure that all the different APIs under the solution group you've subcribed to can be found under the personal API catalog section. This is to show all the specific endpoints you've subscribed to use. **Step 4**: Next is accessiAre Pool Account and Settlement Account configured? Is the Wallet API subscription fully activated? Are there any account-level restrictions? Can they provide test BVN/NIN numbers with known names for testing? Are there additional required fields or validations?ng the TEST API Keys and credentials to be able to test the different APIs here on the sandbox environment (Postman). On the portal, go to the "Developer" Module to access the API Keys. Below contains the: - Client Secret - Client ID - Test environment base URL ([https://baas.dev.getrova.co.uk/](https://baas.dev.getrova.co.uk/)) **Step 5**: Use the Client Secret and Client ID gotten on the dashboard to generate Token on here postman **Note**: this is the API URL to call on Sandbox Test Environment: [https://baas.dev.getrova.co.uk/token](https://baas.dev.getrova.co.uk/)

item.name: Fund Transfer

request.description: ### Request **destinationAccount**: _string required_ Account tp credit the amont into. Must be 10 numeric characters --- **destinationBankCode**: _string required_ The NIBBS code of the destinationAccount. Must be 6 numberic characters --- **amount**: _string required_ Amount to credit destinationAccount in major unit . Must be numeric and takes up to 2 decimal places. **clientReference**: _string optional_ --- A reference to uniquely identify the request. If supplied, must be between 10 and 50 characters. If not supplied, one will be generated and returned in the response. **narration**: _string optional_ --- A description of this request. It must not be more than 20 characters. ### Response _**status**__**__**__: string enum_ Validation status of the request. Determins whether the request format or structure is correct. It is one of `SUCCESS` or `ERROR`. --- **data**: _object_ Contains actual detail about the status of the operation that was performed. Check here for the status of the operation itself --- **message**: _string_ validation message **errors**: _\[string\]_ An array of string stating the validation errors in the request. One of `BAD_REQUEST`, `UNAUTHORIZED` or `FORBIDDEN`. Only present when status is `ERROR`. **messages**: _\[string\]_ --- An array of validation error messages. Only present when status is `ERROR`. ### data object **status**: _string enum_ Actual status of the operation. It is one of `SUCCESSFUL`,`PENDING` or `FAILED`. --- **reference**: _string_ An identifier for the transfer. It can be used to query the status of the transfer at any time. --- **code**: _string enum_ Response code for the transfer. It is an enum of `StatusCodes`. Possible values are provided [here](#codes). --- **message**: _string_ Additional message describing the `code`. --- StatusCodes `SUCCESS`: Success `STATUS_UNKNOWN`: Status unknown, please wait for settlement report `INVALID_SENDER`: Invalid Sender `DO_NOT_HONOR`: Do not honor `DORMANT_ACCOUNT`: Dormant Account `INVALID_ACCOUNT`: Invalid Account `PENDING`: Request processing in progress `INVALID_AMOUNT`: Invalid Amount `INVALID_BATCH_NUMBER`: Invalid Batch Number `INVALID_SESSION_RECORD_ID`: Invalid Session or Record ID `UNKNOWN_BANK_CODE`: Unknown Bank Code `WRONG_METHOD_CALL`: Wrong Method Call `NO_ACTION_TAKEN`: No action taken `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`: Unable to locate record `DUPLICATE_RECORD`: Duplicate record `FORMAT_ERROR`: Format error `SUSPECTED_FRAUD`: Suspected fraud `CONTACT_SENDING_BANK`: Contact sending bank `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`: Insufficient funds `TRANSACTION_NOT_PERMITTED_SENDER`: Transaction not permitted to sender `TRANSACTION_NOT_PERMITTED_CHANNEL`: Transaction not permitted on channel `TRANSFER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`: Transfer limit Exceeded `SECURITY_VIOLATION`: Security violation `EXCEEDS_WITHDRAWAL_FREQUENCY`: Exceeds withdrawal frequency `RESPONSE_RECEIVED_LATE`: Response received too late `EMPTY_MANDATE_REFERENCE_NUMBER`: Empty Mandate Reference Number `BENEFICIARY_BANK_NOT_AVAILABLE`: Beneficiary Bank not available `ROUTING_ERROR`: Routing error `DUPLICATE_TRANSACTION`: Duplicate transaction `SYSTEM_MALFUNCTION`: System malfunction `DESTINATION_TIMEOUT`: Timeout waiting for response from destination `NOT_FOUND`: Not found `EXPIRED`: Expired `EMPTY_VALUE`: Empty value `INVALID_VALUE`: Invalid value `INVALID_DATA_PROVIDED`: Invalid data provided `INVALID_CLIENT_ID`: Invalid client ID `UNABLE_PROCESS_REQUEST`: Unable to process request, please try again `UNKNOWN_ERROR`: Unknown Error `TRANSACTION_ERROR`: There was an error during the transaction. Please do a status check. `ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`: Originator account number not found --- ### Interpreting the Response
Check status of a transfer using the `clientReference` in transfer request or the `reference` response. The response is the same as that of Fund Transfer

item.description:
## **Overview**

The **Collection Account Statement Export API** allows merchants to request a **CSV export** of all **successful** inflows and outflows of transactions from your **Collection Account** within a given date range.

After the API is triggered, the system generates a **CSV file** and delivers it to the **workspace owner's registered email address** for download.

This enables **reconciliation, reporting, and financial tracking**.

## **Email Delivery (CSV Export)**

The workspace account owner will receive an email containing an attachment of the CSV file.

**CSV Columns include:**

- Transaction Date
    
- Collection Account Number
    
- Account Name
    
- Transaction Type (`credit` / `debit`)
    
- Transaction Amount
    
- BaaS Reference
    
- Description
    

**Note on Sandbox Environment:**

In the sandbox environment, email delivery is **not guaranteed**. If an API call returns a `SUCCESS` response, you can be assured that in production an email would be delivered.

To avoid unnecessary costs, we do not send actual test emails from sandbox.

**Alternative Option:**

Instead of relying on emails, you can remove the `/export` in the URL to retrieve the response in JSON format. The contents of this JSON are exactly what would be included in the email in production.

This API is particularly useful in scenarios where network interruptions, timeouts, or delayed responses occur — enabling merchants to confirm whether a transaction was **successful**, **failed**

item.description: Webhooks are a way to recieve real-time notifications of events on Rova BaaS. This allows you to automate tasks and workflows based on different events such as when a Wallet is created, upgraded, credited, debited etc and also when a Virtual account is created, credited or closed. ### **To set up webhooks** - **Step 1**: Go to your Rova BaaS Merchant Portal and navigate to the "Developer" module - **Step 2:** Under the Developer module, navigate to the Webooks section to enable and your register Webhook by clikcing on the toggle. - **Step 3:** Click on the "Register Test Webhook URL" button to open up a modal for you to select the event types you want to recieve notification. - **Step 4:** Once the webhook modal pop up, input the Test Webhook URL and Secret Key (optional) - **Step 5:** Select the events you want to recieve updates for or you can subcribe to all events if you're using both the Wallet and Account services. - **Step 6**: After subcribing to the events, click "Save". You should see the Webhook URL(s) you've registered to for event delivery. **Webhook Delivery Events** This section on the dashboard shows all the webhook events that have been delivered to your webhook URL. In this section you can see the true state of all webhook events as either **SUCCESS** or **RETRY_EXHAUSTED** Each webhook notification has the follwoing event details delivered to your webhook URL: - Event Name e.g: VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT.CREDITED - Status: e.g: SUCCESS - Checksum e.g: 0418a9ffa64bf56094389842e8b2cdb73168f98bf6dcc33e6a4002a5d88ed124 - Created At and Last Updated Time and Date - Retires - Webhook URL the event was sent to - Payload ## **Webhook Event Object** ### Attributes **event** _string_ Contains the name of the event (for example VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT.CREDITED) **id** _string_ Unique identifier for the event **time** _string_ Stringified timestamp of the event time. All time are in UTC. **apiVersion** _string_ The version of BaaS api used to render `data`. **data** _object_ Object containing event data. ## **Webhook Events Types** Below is a comprehensive list of event types that we currently support. Please note that we may introduce additional event types at any time, so it's essential to design your code with flexibility in mind. Our events adhere to a consistent pattern: `RESOURCE.ACTION`. This design aims to provide a predictable and intuitive system for developers. Events are only sent if you have subscribed and a webhook is configured to listen for them. ### **Events Types** ##### **VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT.CREATED** Sent when a new Virtual account is created either Static Virtual account or Dynamic virtual account. #### _data_ **creationTime** _string_ Stringified timestamp of the period the virtual account was created in UTC. **expirationTime** _string_ Stringified timestamp of the period the virtual account was will expire in UTC. Not present if **type** is `STATIC`. amont String Amount tied to the virtual account. Not present if **type** is `STATIC.` **accountNumber** _string_ Account number associated withe the virtual account **name** _string_ Name on the virtual account **type** _string_ Type of the virtual account. One of `STATIC`, `DYNAMIC`. _Sample_ ``` json { "type": "VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT.CREATED", "id": "81903340-e0d7-4c77-a51c-39715dbe39a6", "time": "1738911544", "apiVersion": "1.0", "data": { "creationTime": "1738911544", "expirationTime": "1738911798" "accountNumber": "7000021586", "name": "Fft Non", "amount": "200", "type": "DYNAMIC" } } ``` ##### VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT.CREDITED Sent when a virtual account recieves a payment from external account. #### _data_ **amount** _string_ Amount of the credit in major unit. **accountNumber** _string_ Account number associated with the virtual account. **type** _string_ Type of the virtual account. One of STATIC, DYNAMIC. **senderAccountNumber** _string_ Account number of the originator account **senderAccountName** _string_ Account name on the originator account **senderBank** _string_ Nibbs bank code of the originator account. **time** _string_ Stringified timestamp of the period the credit was received. **reference** _string_ Unique identifier for the credit. _Sample_ ``` json { "type": "VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT.CREDITED", "id": "431f0c6d-2ec7-4a52-b853-6eab40360293", "time": "1738911837", "apiVersion": "1.0", "data": { "amount": "100.0", "accountNumber": "7000021586", "type": "STATIC", "senderAccountNumber": "4518560696", "senderAccountName": "Jamie Dust", "senderBank": "000014", "time": "1738911837", "reference": "seNpppbPSTk" } } ``` ##### **WALLET.CREATED** Sent when a new wallet account is created. #### _data_ **name** _string_ Name on the wallet. **time** _string_ Stringified timestamp of when the wallet was created in UTC. **tier** _string_ The account tier of the wallet. One of ONE, TWO ,THREE. **accountNumber** _string_ Account number associated with the wallet. **status** _string_ Current state of the wallet. One of ACTIVE, FROZEN, CLOSED, LIENED, CREDIT_BLOCKED, DEBIT_BLOCKED _Sample_ ``` json { "type": "WALLET.CREATED", "id": "de431dad-b6d8-4db2-9ad1-d46c81d56cc7", "time": "1738912472", "apiVersion": "1.0", "data": { "name": "Leo John", "time": "1738912472", "tier": "ONE", "accountNumber": "4000021592", "status": "ACTIVE" } } ``` ##### **WALLET.STATUS_CHANGED** Sent when a particualr wallet account's status changes from one state to another (e.g Frozen,, Liened/Unliend, Debit Blocked/Debit UnBlocked, Closed) #### _data_ **name** _string_ Name on the wallet. **time** _string_ Stringified timestamp of when the wallet was created in UTC. **tier** _string_ The account tier of the wallet. One of ONE, TWO ,THREE. **accountNumber** _string_ Account number associated with the wallet. **status** _string_ Current state of the wallet. One of ACTIVE, FROZEN, CLOSED, LIENED, CREDIT_BLOCKED, DEBIT_BLOCKED _Sample_ ``` json { "type": "WALLET.STATUS_CHANGED", "id": "de431dad-b6d8-4db2-9ad1-d46c81d5defr", "time": "1738912472", "apiVersion": "1.0", "data": { "name": "Leo John", "time": "1738912472", "tier": "ONE", "accountNumber": "4000021592", "status": "CLOSED" } } ``` ##### **WALLET.UPGRADED** Sent when a wallet account is upgraded from one tier to another tier. #### _data_ **name** _string_ Name on the wallet. **time** _string_ Stringified timestamp of when the wallet was created in UTC. **tier** _string_ The account tier of the wallet. One of `ONE`, `TWO` ,`THREE`. **accountNumber** _string_ Account number associated with the wallet. **status** _string_ Current state of the wallet. One of `ACTIVE`, `FROZEN`, `CLOSED`, `LIENED`, `CREDIT_BLOCKED`, `DEBIT_BLOCKED` _Sample_ ``` json { "type": "WALLET.UPGRADED", "id": "de431dad-b6d8-4db2-9ad1-d46c81d5aesc", "time": "1738912472", "apiVersion": "1.0", "data": { "name": "Leo John", "time": "1738912472", "tier": "THREE", "accountNumber": "4000021592", "status": "ACTIVE" } } ``` ##### **WALLET.CREDITED** Sent when a particular wallet account receives a payment. #### _data_ **amount** _string_ Amount of the credit in major unit. **accountNumber** _string_ Account number associated with the wallet. **senderAccountNumber** _string_ Account number of the originator account **senderAccountName** _string_ Account name on the originator account **senderBank** _string_ Nibbs bank code of the originator account. **time** _string_ Stringified timestamp of the period the credit was received. **reference** _string_ Unique identifier for the credit. **scope** _string_ Type of the credit. One of `WALLET_TO_WALLET`, `WALLET_TO_BANK` , `BANK_TO_WALLET` Sample ``` json { "type": "WALLET.CREDITED", "id": "431f0c6d-2ec7-4a52-b853-6eab4032derf", "time": "1738911837", "apiVersion": "1.0", "data": { "amount": "100.0", "accountNumber": "4000021586", "senderAccountNumber": "4518560696", "senderAccountName": "Jamie Dust", "senderBank": "000014", "time": "1738911837", "reference": "seNpppbPSTk", "scope": "BANK_TO_WALLET" } } ``` ##### **WALLET.DEBITED** Sent when a particular wallet account makes a payment. #### data **amount** _string_ Amount of the debit in major unit. **accountNumber** _string_ Account number associated with the wallet. **beneficiary** _string_ Account number of the beneficiary. **beneficiaryBank** _string_ Nibbs bank code of the beneficiary bank. Not present if scope is `WALLET_TO_WALLET.` **time** _string_ Stringified timestamp of the period the credit was received. **reference** _string_ Unique identifier for the credit. **scope** _string_ Type of the credit. One of `WALLET_TO_WALLET`, `WALLET_TO_BANK` , `BANK_TO_WALLET` _Sample_ ``` json "type": "WALLET.CREDITED", "id": "431f0c6d-2ec7-4a52-b853-6eab4032derf", "time": "1738911837", "apiVersion": "1.0", "data": { "amount": "100.0", "accountNumber": "4000021586", "beneficiary": "4000032124", "beneficiaryBank": "000003", "time": "1738911837", "reference": "seNpppbPSTk", "scope": "WALLET_TO_BANK" } } ``` ##### **FUND_TRANSFER.COMPLETED** Sent when a fundtransfer finishes (succeeds or fails). #### data **status** _string_ Status of the transfer. One of `FAILED` or `SUCCESSFUL`. **code**: _string enum_ Response code for the transfer. It is an enum of `StatusCodes`. Possible values are provided [here](#codes). **sourceAccount** _string_ Account number which was debited **sourceBankCode** _string_ Nibbs bank code of the source account bank. **destinationAccount** _string_ Account number of the beneficiary. **destinationBankCode** _string_ Nibbs bank code of the beneficiary bank. **Amount** _string_ Amount of the transfer. **reference** _string_ Unique identifier for the transfer. **narration** _string_ Narration/Remark for the transfer. **message** _string_ Message descrbing the status. **time** _string_ Stringified timestamp of the period the credit was received. ``` json { "type": "FUND_TRANSFER.COMPLETED", "id": "a37f64ff-74cd-4f1a-bb81-67b9091355a3", "time": "1750862803", "apiVersion": "1.0", "data": { "status": "SUCCESSFUL", "code": "SUCCESS", "sourceAccount": "2483520014", "sourceBankCode": "000003", "destinationAccount": "3409329879", "destinationBankCode": "089070", "amount": "510.10", "reference": "NL47RGAP5468750058", "narration": "Transfer to mut", "message": "Approved or Completed Successfully", "time": "2025-05-25T14:46:43.152622727" } } ``` ``` json { "type": "FUND_TRANSFER.COMPLETED", "id": "a37f64ff-74cd-4f1a-bb81-67b90454sde0", "time": "1748166040", "apiVersion": "1.0", "data": { "status": "FAILED", "code": "DORMANT_ACCOUNT", "sourceAccount": "2483520090", "sourceBankCode": "000003", "destinationAccount": "1308329879", "destinationBankCode": "090097", "amount": "3000.50", "reference": "NL59RGAP5468750987", "narration": "Thanks for transfer", "message": "Dormant Account", "time": "2025-05-25T19:40:40.152622727" } } ``` ### Webhook Delivery and Handling #### **Sending Back Response** You are expected to return a **2xx** HTTP response to every message received as quickly as possible. Any other status will be deemed as failure. Defer any complex processing that could cause a timeout until _after_ sending this initial response. This can also help increase the scalablility of your webhook endpoint. #### Retries In test mode, we try to deliver a specific event to your webhook endpoint 3 times over the course of a few hours. In live mode, we attempt delivery for up to 72 hours, using an exponential back-off strategy. ##### Event Order We do not guarantee that events will be delivered in the order they are generated. Your endpoint should not rely on these events being delivered in a specific order and must handle deliveries appropriately. ##### Duplicates Your endpoint may occassionally receive duplicate events . To prevent processing the same event multiple times, you can maintain a log of the event IDs that have already been handled, and skip any events with IDs that are already in the log. To identify these duplicates, use the `id` field of the event object along with the `type` field. **Validating Received Webhook** To ensure the integrity and authenticity of webhooks sent by our platform, we include a signature with each payload. This allows you to verify that the webhook originated from us and hasn't been tampered with during transit. The hash is computed using the **secret key** that you see on your webhook page on the your dashboard and included in the request header as `X-checksum-hash`. You are expected to: - Extract the `X-Hash` header from the incoming webhook request - Re-calculate the hash using HMACSHA256 with the secret key. - Compare your calculated hash with the one in the `X-checksum-hash` header. - If the hashes do not match, reject request. **Example Validation in Python** ``` python import hmac import hashlib import json client_secret_key = b'YOUR_WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY' payload = json.dumps(request.json, separators=(',', ':')).encode('utf-8') # Raw JSON payload computed_hash = hmac.new(client_secret_key, payload, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest() ``` **Example Validation in JavaScript** ``` javascript const crypto = require('crypto'); const clientSecretKey = 'YOUR_WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY'; const payload = JSON.stringify(requestBody); // Ensure this is the raw payload const computedHash = crypto.createHmac('sha256', clientSecretKey).update(payload).digest('hex'); ```

item.name: NIN Verification
item.description:
## Overview

This API is available as both as a `Synchronous API` and an `Asynchronous API`. The `Asynchronous API` allows an eventual response. The `Synchronous API` is suited for real-time environments.

Use this API to do:

- **NIN Verification Match**: This API allows you to get very simple or `basic` NIN information about a customer.
- **NIN Verification**: This API allows you to get more or `enhanced` NIN information about a customer.
- **NIN Biometric**: This API allows you to verify the ID information of your user and confirm that the ID actually belongs to the user, this is achieved by comparing the user's liveness images and a primary image to either the photo of the user on file in an ID authority database or a photo of their ID card.
- **Async Endpoints**: These APIs take a `callbackurl` which is your webhook endpoint. The verification response will be sent to the provided `callbackurl`.

item.name: Utility Bill Verification

formdata.description: Image of utility bill to verify. Image file must not be more than 5MB
The city in which the adress on the utility bill is located
The state in Nigeria, which the adress on the utility bill is located. Should be in CAPITAL letters.
The local government area in which the adress on the utility bill is located.
The phone number of owner of the utility bill. Compulsory

request.description:
##### Request Parameters:

- image: **Required**. Clear picture of utility. Should not be more than 5MB.
    
- city: **Required**. City in which the address on the utility bill is located.
    
- state: **Required**. One of `ABIA, ADAMAWA, AKWA IBOM, ANAMBRA, BAUCHI, BAYELSA, BENUE, BORNO, CROSS RIVER, DELTA, EBONYI, EDO, EKITI, ENUGU, GOMBE, IMO, JIGAWA, KADUNA, KANO, KATSINA, KEBBI, KOGI, KWARA, LAGOS, NASARAWA, NIGER, OGUN, ONDO, OSUN, OYO, PLATEAU, RIVERS, SOKOTO, TARABA, YOBE, ZAMFARA, FCT`. Must be in **CAPITAL** letters.
    
- lga: **Required**. Local Government Area in which the address on the utility bill is located.
    
- phone: **Required**. Phone number of the owner of the utility bill.
    

##### Understanding the Response

Descrbing the **data** field:

- status: **string**. can only have SUCCESS has its value.
    
- reference: **string**. Use this check the status of the verification with the `check status` API.

request.description:
##### Request Parameters:

- id: **Required.** the reference that was obtained in the response fo the `Verify Utility Bill` API **.**
    

##### Understanding the response field

Descrbing the **data** field:

- status: **string**. one of `PROCESSING`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `DATE_NOT_FOUND`, `DATE_TOO_OLD`, `ADDRESS_NOT_READABLE`, `ADDRESS_NOT_VALID`
    
- utilityDate: **string**. contains the date extracted from the utility bill
    
- utilityAgeInMonths: **string**. contains the number of months elapsed between the date on the utility bill and when it was submitted for validation.
    
- utilityAddress: **string**. address extracted from the utility bill.
    
- utilityAddressLocated: **boolean**. true if the address on the utility bill was successfully located, otherwise false.
    
- utilityAddressLongitude: **string.** contains the longitutude of the address on the utility bill.
    
- utilityAddressLatitude: **string.** contains the latitude of the address on the utility bill.
    
- message: describe the status.
    

##### Descrbing the different statuses

- PROCESSING : the validation process is still ongoing.
    
- COMPLETED: the validation process has completed successfully without errors. All fields are present.
    
- FAILED: the validation process failed due to a processing error. You would have to retry the process.
    
- DATE_NOT_FOUND: date on the utility bill could not be read, or there's no date on the utility bill. You would have to check the utility bill has a date field that is conspicous or take a clearer higher resolution image of the utility bill.
    
- DATE_TOO_OLD: date on the utility is older than 3months. You would have to use another image that is less the 3months old.
    
- ADDRESS_NOT_READABLE: address on the utility bill could not be read, or there's no address on the utility bill. You would have to check the utility bill has an address field that is conspicous or take a clearer higher resolution image of the utility bill.
    
- ADDRESS_NOT_VALID: address extracted on the utility bill could not be located. You would have to use another utility bill with a valid address.
    

**NB**: check out the examples in the request specifications, all these states are shown as examples there.

item.description:
This API allows you to `Verify Utility Bills` with an image not greater than 5MB. When you submit the request, the API returns a reference with which you query the `check status` API to get the result of the validation.

##### Understanding The Response

Response Fields:

- **status**: either `SUCCESS` or `ERROR`. `SUCCESS` means the API call was successful. **Does not** necessarily mean the actual business operation was successful. E.g it does not necessarily mean the utility bill submitted passed all validations, look to the `data` field for that info. `ERROR` indicates there's an error in the request submitted by the client or a server error occured while parsing the request.
    
- **data**: contains the result of the business operation. This is where you will find the response of the validation; if the utility bill passed all validations or failed. Not present when status is `ERROR`.
    
- **errors**: contains an array of all client request errors. E.g. if the image or city field is missing, this array contains that information. Not present when status is `SUCCESS`.
    
- **message**: describes the status. Always `success` for `SUCCESS` status. Not present when status is `ERROR`.
    
- **messages**: an array describing the contents of the errors field. Not present when status is `SUCCESS`.

## Overview

This API is available as both as a `Synchronous API` and an `Asynchronous API`. The `Asynchronous API` allows an eventual response. The `Synchronous API` is suited for real-time environments.

Use this API to do:

- **Business Verification Match**: This API allows you to get very simple or `basic` business registration information.
    
- **Business Verification Verification**: This API allows you to get more or `enhanced` business registration information.
    
- **Tax Verification**: This API allows you to verify tax information of your user.
    
- **Async Endpoints**: These APIs take a `callbackurl` which is your webhook endpoint. The verification response will be sent to the provided `callbackurl`.

item.description:
## **Overview**

The **Collection Account Statement Export API** allows merchants to request a **CSV export** of all **successful** inflows and outflows of transactions from your **Collection Account** within a given date range.

After the API is triggered, the system generates a **CSV file** and delivers it to the **workspace owner's registered email address** for download.

This enables **reconciliation, reporting, and financial tracking**.

## **Email Delivery (CSV Export)**

The workspace account owner will receive an email containing an attachment of the CSV file.

**CSV Columns include:**

- Transaction Date
    
- Collection Account Number
    
- Account Name
    
- Transaction Type (`credit` / `debit`)
    
- Transaction Amount
    
- BaaS Reference
    
- Description
    

**Note on Sandbox Environment:**  
  
In the sandbox environment, email delivery is **not guaranteed**. If an API call returns a `SUCCESS` response, you can be assured that in production an email would be delivered.

To avoid unnecessary costs, we do not send actual test emails from sandbox.

**Alternative Option:**

  
Instead of relying on emails, you can remove the `/export` in the URL to retrieve the response in JSON format. The contents of this JSON are exactly what would be included in the email in production.

item.description:
| **Backend Errors** | **Error Code** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | 500 | Something went wrong on our end. Please retry or contact support if it persists. |
|  | 401 | Unauthorized request. Check your API key, secret token, or credentials and try again. |
|  | 404 | Request could not be fulfilled as the request resource does not exist. |
|  | 503 | Service temporarily unavailable. Please retry after some time. |
|  | 400 | Invalid request. Check required fields or parameters and try again. |
|  | 504 | The request took too long to respond. Please try again. If the problem persists, reach out to support. |
|  |  |  |
| **Frontend Errors** | Organiation does not exist | You need to add your collection account if using the Virtual account service or Add your Settlement. |
|  | An Error Occured, try again | Request could not be fulfilled due to an error on our end. Please retry after some time. |
|  | Failed to Load resource | Request could not be fulfilled due to an error on our end. Please retry after some time. |
|  | No static resource/create merchant | An unexpected error occurred during the request. Please, contact [baas@fcmb.com](https://mailto:baas@fcmb.com) |
|  | Required header 'x-request-id is not present | An unexpected error occurred during the request. Please, contact [baas@fcmb.com](https://mailto:baas@fcmb.com) |
|  | Invalid Scheme Code | The account number you're trying to use isn't supported for collections on FCMB BaaS. Please contact our support team at [baas@fcmb.com](https://mailto:baas@fcmb.com) to help you set up a valid account number with the correct configuration for collections. |

All BaaS API is RESTful and as such, uses conventional HTTP response codes to indicate the success or failure of requests.
